Raw: The loss against SA had nothing to do with stadiums, infrastructure, or investments. That was a disgraceful display of batting and an embarrassing run chase. It's about time we stopped hiding behind the excuse of "learning from this loss." That was an utterly pathetic performance. Scoring 36 runs off 42 balls with 8 wickets in hand doesn't require an international stadium in Nepal—it requires basic competence. Fans need to start asking tough questions instead of constantly trying to find silver linings. If we keep looking for positives in every defeat, we will just keep losing. BTW Hami early 2000 dekhi Professional Cricket khelna thale ko team ho, we are not Mongolia or Uganda. This was our 2nd T20 WC appearance, we have played 100s of matches with good teams over the years. The fans need to have the balls to criticize when it's wrong. We as a fans must wake this team into reality else Bhutan ra Mongolia sanga series kheldai base huncha next 10 years pani. Post-Match Conference hereko, Rohit said "we played great as a unit in both bowling and batting", I mean wt;;;;f. Laaaj bhanne kura chaina ???? Entire world saw how we gave away a well set game because of poor batting, planning and judgement. WC ayeko compete garna lai ho, hamro so called learning phase is/was over 5 years ago.

Raw: I did this trek solo in October, 2006 with a porter and guide where both were paid a daily rate. I also had to pay their flights to/from Lukla, but their fares were half of mine. I wanted to go at my own pace to avoid any AMS. 10 days out but 4 days back. I was 57 y/o. I spent a week in KTM around the trek, including a 3-day homestay. I don't remember the cost exactly, but I was probably around $2K back then. No WiFi on the trail. I had an SLR camera that ran with AAA batteries.
